WorldFloraFast: fast standardization of plant names against the World Flora Online

Source: R/WorldFloraFast-package.R
WorldFloraFast-package.Rd

Matches plant names against a static copy of the World Flora Online (WFO) taxonomic backbone, exactly or with fuzzy matching, and finds the currently accepted names. WorldFloraFast is a faster, refactored derivative of the WorldFlora package (Kindt 2020); functions and arguments are the same.

Workflow

  1. Obtain the backbone with WFO.download() (later sessions: WFO.remember() or WFO.read()).

  2. Optionally split full names with authors via WFO.prepare().

  3. Match names with WFO.match().

  4. Keep one match per submitted name with WFO.one().

  5. Explore with WFO.browse(), WFO.synonyms(), WFO.family() and WFO.url(); check whether fuzzy matches are explained by misspellings with WFO.spelling.check().

Other taxonomic lists can be used as backbone via WFO.backbone().

Speed

The backbone is indexed once per call, so that exact matches, accepted names and genera are found with hash lookups. Fuzzy matching is done once per distinct name, optionally in parallel (argument cores), and each agrep() search is preceded by an exact prefilter (see WFO.match()). Results are those of WorldFlora 1.14-5, apart from the corrections listed in the NEWS file (news(package = "WorldFloraFast")).

Compatibility with WorldFlora

By default, functions behave as in WorldFlora 1.14-5: same arguments, defaults, result columns (names, order, types) and example data set. Only errors of WorldFlora are corrected (listed in the NEWS file); in WFO.match(), three of these corrections can be switched off (Fuzzy.keep.genus, Fuzzy.epithet.check, Fuzzy.skip.placeholder). The matching steps added by WorldFloraFast (Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer, Fuzzy.one.strict) are optional and switched off by default.

Cache

The index of the backbone and the context used by the matching steps (about 5 s to build for the 1.6 million names of the WFO Plant List 2026-06) are kept for the last backbone used, so that further calls with the same WFO.data take a fraction of a second. This works when WFO.data is a data.table, as returned by WFO.read() (a data.frame is copied at each call). A changed backbone is detected. Set options(WorldFloraFast.cache = FALSE) to switch the cache off.

Deprecated

WFO.match.fuzzyjoin(), WFO.acceptable.match() (replaced by WFO.spelling.check()) and the argument no.dates of WFO.match() still work, with a warning, and will be removed in a later version.

Provenance

WorldFloraFast is derived from WorldFlora 1.14-5 (Roeland Kindt, GPL-3). Each R source file of the package starts with a caption that lists what it inherits from WorldFlora, what was changed, and what is new; the NEWS file lists all changes of results.

References

Kindt, R. (2020). WorldFlora: An R package for exact and fuzzy matching of plant names against the World Flora Online taxonomic backbone data. Applications in Plant Sciences 8(9): e11388. doi:10.1002/aps3.11388

World Flora Online. An Online Flora of All Known Plants. https://www.worldfloraonline.org
